# iNaturalist adapter spike — R9 findings (M0, throwaway)

*Generated by `tools/spike-inat/run-spike.mjs` on a stratified 20-name sample from
`corpus-201.csv`. Read-only, unauthenticated, throttled ~0.8 rps. Feeds milestone
M3 (licensing) + M4 (name reconciliation) + M5 (CV gate). Numbers are one point-in-
time sample, not a contract.*

## TL;DR

- **Name resolution:** **11/20** names hit on the **raw** `scientificName`; normalizing decorated names (strip `'Cultivar'` / `(parenthetical)` / `×` → bare binomial) recovered **8** more, for **19/20** total. Every raw miss was a **cultivar/trade/hybrid-decorated** string — plain binomials and mosses hit 1:1. This is the single most important M4 finding: **strip to the binomial before querying, keep our cultivar string locally.**
- **Synonyms are real:** `Calathea ornata` → `Goeppertia ornata` — the external name can differ from ours at the genus level, so M4 must store the returned canonical name, not assume ours matches.
- **Licensing:** default-photo license distribution below is a **mix of CC-BY-NC / CC0 / all-rights-reserved** — "just pull iNat photos" is not a blanket yes; commercial reuse in particular is largely blocked.
- **CV:** `computervision/score_image` returned **HTTP 401** unauthenticated — it requires auth (answer, not assumption); an M5 gate input.
- **API version:** v1 returns full objects; **v2 returns almost nothing without an explicit `fields` selection** (1 key(s) bare vs 4 with `fields`) — the adapter must send v2 field trees or use v1.
- **Rate/cache:** median latency 102 ms; header findings in §5–6.

## 1. Name resolution (q1)

Per-stratum **raw** hit rate (querying the corpus `scientificName` verbatim) vs
**normalized** hit rate (after the strip-to-binomial ladder):

| Stratum | Raw hit rate | Normalized hit rate |
|---|---|---|
| plain-species | 5/5 (100%) | 5/5 (100%) |
| cultivar-suffixed | 1/5 (20%) | 4/5 (80%) |
| trade-or-hybrid | 0/5 (0%) | 5/5 (100%) |
| moss-or-ally | 5/5 (100%) | 5/5 (100%) |

Full sample (normalized column shows the query that recovered a raw miss):

| slug | stratum | raw | normalized | matched name | rank | default photo license |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fittonia-albivenis | plain-species | ✓ | — | Fittonia albivenis | species | — |
| soleirolia-soleirolii | plain-species | ✓ | — | Soleirolia soleirolii | species | cc-by-nc |
| maranta-leuconeura | plain-species | ✓ | — | Maranta leuconeura | species | cc-by-nc |
| calathea-ornata | plain-species | ✓ | — | Goeppertia ornata | species | — |
| hypoestes-phyllostachya | plain-species | ✓ | — | Hypoestes phyllostachya | species | cc0 |
| selaginella-kraussiana | cultivar-suffixed | ✗ | ✓ via `Selaginella kraussiana` | Selaginella kraussiana | species | — |
| scindapsus-pictus-argyraeus | cultivar-suffixed | ✓ | — | Scindapsus pictus argyraeus | variety | — |
| alocasia-reginula-black-velvet | cultivar-suffixed | ✗ | ✓ via `Alocasia reginula` | Alocasia reginula | species | cc-by-nc |
| ficus-pumila-panama | cultivar-suffixed | ✗ | ✓ via `Ficus pumila` | Ficus pumila | species | — |
| peperomia-orba-pixie-lime | cultivar-suffixed | ✗ | ✗ | — | — | — |
| crassula-ovata-mini | trade-or-hybrid | ✗ | ✓ via `Crassula ovata` | Crassula ovata | species | cc-by-nc-nd |
| anubias-nana-petite | trade-or-hybrid | ✗ | ✓ via `Anubias barteri` | Anubias barteri | species | pd |
| neoregelia-hybrid-liliputiana | trade-or-hybrid | ✗ | ✓ via `Neoregelia` | Neoregelia | genus | cc-by-nc |
| alocasia-amazonica-bambino | trade-or-hybrid | ✗ | ✓ via `Alocasia amazonica` | Alocasia | genus | cc-by-nc |
| nephrolepis-exaltata-fluffy-ruffles | trade-or-hybrid | ✗ | ✓ via `Nephrolepis exaltata` | Nephrolepis exaltata | species | cc-by-nc |
| leucobryum-glaucum | moss-or-ally | ✓ | — | Leucobryum glaucum | species | cc-by-nc |
| dicranum-scoparium | moss-or-ally | ✓ | — | Dicranum scoparium | species | — |
| taxiphyllum-barbieri | moss-or-ally | ✓ | — | Taxiphyllum barbieri | species | cc-by-nc |
| sphagnum-palustre | moss-or-ally | ✓ | — | Sphagnum palustre | species | cc-by-nc |
| selaginella-uncinata | moss-or-ally | ✓ | — | Selaginella uncinata | species | cc-by-nc |

**Reading it.** iNat's taxonomy stops at species / subspecies / variety — named
horticultural cultivars are not ranks — and autocomplete does **not** fuzzily ignore a
`'Cultivar'`, parenthetical, or `×` in the query; it simply misses. Stripping to the
bare binomial recovers those hits at rank `species`. So M4's matched / ambiguous /
cultivar / unmatched report must:
1. **Normalize before querying** (drop cultivar quotes, parentheticals, hybrid marks; fall back to genus+species).
2. Treat "cultivar → species" as **matched-with-loss**, keeping our own cultivar string beside the external species id (ADR 0022: external id is a reference, never the key).
3. Store the **returned canonical name** (synonyms like Calathea→Goeppertia mean ours can be an outdated synonym).
4. Expect a residual unmatched tail (obscure hybrids/trade names) needing manual curation.

## 2. Licensing reality (q2)

Default-photo license across the 19 hits:

- `cc-by-nc`: 10
- `null(ARR/none)`: 6
- `cc0`: 1
- `cc-by-nc-nd`: 1
- `pd`: 1

Top-photo licenses across 6 `taxa/{id}` detail calls (36 photos):

- `null`: 16
- `cc-by-nc`: 9
- `cc-by`: 3
- `cc0`: 3
- `cc-by-nc-nd`: 2
- `cc-by-sa`: 2
- `cc-by-nc-sa`: 1

**M3 takeaway:** license is **per-photo**, not per-taxon — a taxon can have a CC0
default and ARR alternates (or vice-versa). The adapter must read `license_code` on
each photo and filter, never assume a taxon-level license. `null` = all-rights-
reserved (unusable without permission). Attribution (`attribution`,
`attribution_name`) travels per photo and must be surfaced wherever a licensed image
is shown (ADR 0024).

## 3. Observations aggregate (q3)

- `fittonia-albivenis` (taxon 327855): status 200, 12 month buckets, 2300 obs, 82 ms.
- `soleirolia-soleirolii` (taxon 79147): status 200, 12 month buckets, 4886 obs, 89 ms.

One `observations/histogram` call per taxon is cheap and gives a month-of-year
phenology curve. Useful as a *popularity/seasonality display signal only* — **never a
care input** (ADR 0023: care data is sourced, not occurrence-derived).

## 4. Computer-vision access (q4)

- `GET /v1/computervision/score_image` → HTTP 404
- `POST /v1/computervision/score_image` (no image, no auth) → HTTP 401 ("Unauthorized")

**Answer:** the CV endpoint is **not anonymously accessible** — it needs an
authenticated iNat API token (and image upload). So M5's CV feature can't assume
free access; either obtain a token under iNat's terms, run our own model, or keep CV
gated **off** (ADR 0025 — CV fails safe to manual selection).

## 5. Rate behavior (q5)

- Latency over 42 calls: min 82 ms · median 102 ms · max 562 ms.
- Rate-limit headers seen: **none exposed** on these endpoints.
- No deliberate 429 was forced (courtesy). iNat documents ~100 req/min and ≤10k/day; at our ~0.8 rps a batch of a few hundred taxa is well within budget. M3 sync should still implement backoff-and-retry on 429 (the client here does one bounded retry).

## 6. Cacheability (q6)

- Cache-related headers seen: `etag`, `cache-control`, `age`, `x-cache`.
- Implication: ETags are present on at least some endpoints — conditional GETs are viable for a local cache. Taxonomy + license data is slow-moving, so generous client-side TTLs (days) are safe; observation aggregates change faster.

## API-version note

v2 autocomplete for `Fittonia albivenis` returned a top result with keys
`[id]` with **no** `fields` param vs
`[id, name, rank, default_photo]` with an explicit field tree. The adapter
(ADR 0022) must either send v2 `fields` selections or use v1's fuller default
objects; this spike used v1 for substance for that reason.
